acceptance: Every failed Trunk push run in a stated 14-day window is classified with run id, failing job and cause, and the table is recorded on this item
Stale-base composition failures are counted and compared with the about-once-a-week threshold; if exceeded, an owner decision on reinstating the up-to-date requirement is requested
Top recurring flake causes each have an item (existing or new) linked here
Trunk push failure rate over the following 14 days is below 2%, or the remaining causes are recorded with owners
context: Source: independent review of the PR-checks versus Trunk split on 2026-10-24 (develop a56738db4; run history 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-24: 465 merges, 466 Trunk push runs, 126 Trunk coverage runs). This sets the baseline that coverage selection needs before going live, since selection misses would surface as Trunk failures.
description: 59 of 466 Trunk push runs on develop (12.7%) failed between 2026-10-10 and 2026-10-24, on 13 of 15 days, each on a different merged PR, but only 2 reverts merged. The documented policy is revert-first with a red-trunk gate on make pr-open, so most reds cleared without action: the signal is diluted by flakes. Classify every red run as flaky, Python 3.12 only (PR fast runs on 3.14, Trunk fast on 3.12), stale-base composition between concurrent squash merges, or real regression. Fix or quarantine the top flakes through their own items (known: trunk-dist-artifact-producer-check-flake-20261022, ci-amplab-generate-data-timeout-flake). Compare the stale-base count with the governance threshold (more than about one a week means reinstating the up-to-date requirement; develop rulesets currently have strict_required_status_checks_policy false and no merge queue).
